item.title: Swinux is attending Orientation and Launch week!
item.description:
Swinux will attend Orientation and Launch week for semester 1 of 2026!

Last week, the club announced that it would be attending launch week on the 25th and 27th of Feburary. Today, we are also confirming that we will be attending Launch week from the 2nd to the 4th of March.

Orientation and Launch week will see the clubs of Swinburne represent themselves to new and returning Swinburne students. The Swinburne Student Association is also hosting free food and interactive activities to get people excited and connected going into Semester 1 of 2026.
item.content:
Swinux will attend Orientation and Launch week for semester 1 of 2026!

Last week, the club announced that it would be attending launch week on the 25th and 27th of Feburary. Today, we are also confirming that we will be attending Launch week from the 2nd to the 4th of March.

Orientation and Launch week will see the clubs of Swinburne represent themselves to new and returning Swinburne students. The Swinburne Student Association is also hosting free food and interactive activities to get people excited and connected going into Semester 1 of 2026.

Throughout the upcoming events, you will get a chance to meet club commitee members, talk about all things tech and learn more about the events and meetups the club are planning for 2026. Plus, the stall will also have Linux/Hardware/Coding themed goodies for you to collect!

If you’re new to Swinux, you can have a look at our previous we’ve held throughout the second half of 2025. As always, we’re keen to hear your feedback and input regarding the direction of the club. You can always get in contact with us through our email, contact@swinux.org, or alternatively via Instagram and .

  • Join our Discord Server

item.title: Annual General Meeting Announced: 4PM 16th of October 2025
item.description:
This Year’s Annual General Meeting (AGM) date is confirmed, and will be held this Thursday 16th of October 2025 @ 4pm. It will be held online via Discord, and elections will be conducted using Rubric.

The AGM will establish the Swinux (Linux Hardware & Code Club) committee for 2026. Nominations for positions are open, closing Friday the 10th @ 5pm. Elections will be held for the Vice President role, with each candidate given time to give a statement before voting commences.
item.content:
This Year’s Annual General Meeting (AGM) date is confirmed, and will be held this Thursday 16th of October 2025 @ 4pm. It will be held online via Discord, and elections will be conducted using Rubric.

The AGM will establish the Swinux (Linux Hardware & Code Club) committee for 2026. Nominations for positions are open, closing Friday the 10th @ 5pm. Elections will be held for the Vice President role, with each candidate given time to give a statement before voting commences.

In order to vote, you must associate your student account with Rubric. This allows you to obtain a membership (free for Swinburne students) and ticket to attend the SGM, which is a requirement for voting. The committee encourages all who are interested in the club to attend and vote.

The club has exciting things in the planning stage for 2026 and beyond. By voting, you help to enable the club to create an environment for you, where your passions for everything Linux, Software and Hardware can be shared in a common space with like minds.

item.content:
That’s a wrap on the inaugural C++ Workshop for Swinux!

President Dylan presenting the C++ Workshop

We hope all that attended in person or remotely had a great time learning about the fundamentals of C++. We have a list of resources hosted on our club GitHub repository should you wish to revisit the workshop, including slides, code and documentation regarding setup on Linux, Windows and Mac:

Find the Workshop materials here

We had a blast covering the following topics:

  • Basics of C++
  • Object-Oriented Programming
  • Memory Management
  • Data Structures
  • Template Meta-Programming

Alternatively, if you’re less interested in learning during the Workshop, the events held by the club provide an excellent opportunity to network with fellow students, learn new technologies and techniques.

Attendee showing the cmatrix effect in the terminal

We’d also like to say a small thank you to President Dylan for his work in hosting the Workshop and preparing all of the materials, and the rest of the committee for their support.

Lastly, if you’re looking out for more in-person events held by the club, keep a look out on our official channels for upcoming announcements. We look forward to seeing you again!

You can find our official channels below:

  • Discord: Swinburne Linux Hardware & Code Club

  • Instagram: @swinburne_lhcc

  • Club Page: Swinburne Linux, Hardware and Code Club

item.content:
We have just announced the first C++ Workshop for Semester 2 of 2025!

Taking place in Week 5, this workshop will focus on explaining the basics to novice to intermediate programmers. This workshop is hosted by the Swinux President, Dylan, who has industry experience with C++. Previous coding experience is recommended, although not neccessary to attend and learn more about programming. The workshop will conduct the following:

  • The Basics of C++
  • Object Orientate Programming
  • Memory Management
  • Data Structure
  • Template Meta-Programming (Advanced)

The workshop will have time for networking before the workshop to get comfortable. A short presentation will be given explaining the core concepts of programming in C++, including a short history of the language. During this time, feel free to seek clarification in setting up or with any questions you may have.

The workshop will cover the basic concepts of C++, implementing several key features of the language. Afterwards, a more advanced workshop will be held for intermediate programmers. Be sure to attend ATC101 on Thursday the 4th of September @ 1:30pm for the full experience!

If you have not yet signed up with club membership, you can do so via the channels below:

  • Rubric Club Signup
  • Join our Discord Server

item.title: SGM Results Semester 2 2025
item.description:
Congratulations to Swinux (the Swinburne Linux Hardware Code Club) for meeting qourum for Semester 2 2025!

Your votes have enabled the club to extend into Semester 2 of 2025. The club has nominated the following club members to the committee:

  • Timothy (Vice President)
  • Oscar (Treasurer)

They will join our President Dylan and Secretary Dani in the committee for Semester 2 of 2025. Congratulations to the candidates, and a thank you for everyone who ran for the committee. We appreciate everyone who helps contribute to keep the club running.
